ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the diagram, three rays emanate from point J, and the pink angle mark indicates that the middle ray bisects this angle. Point S is on the angle bisector. The foot of the perpendicular segment from S to the upper side is M, with the length labeled next to it as 3x+5; the foot of the perpendicular segment from S to the lower horizontal side is P, with the length labeled next to it as 6x-7, and the problem asks to find SP. Reasoning: A point on an angle bisector has equal perpendicular distances to the two sides of the angle, so SM = SP. From the labels in the diagram, 3x+5 = 6x-7 can be obtained. Solve the equation: 3x+5 = 6x-7, 12 = 3x, so x = 4. Substitute into SP = 6x-7 to get SP = 6(4)-7 = 24-7 = 17.

method.method_draft: From the image: the pink angle marks at J show the middle ray is the angle bisector, and the right-angle boxes show S has perpendiculars to the two sides of the angle labeled 3x+5 and 6x-7. The text asks for SP, which is the perpendicular from S to the base. Use the angle-bisector theorem: a point on an angle bisector is equidistant from the sides, so 3x+5 = 6x-7. Solve x = 4, then substitute to get SP = 6x-7 = 17.
